summary: Alabama is simpler than it first looks, straight from the wildlife agency. The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that it does NOT regulate roof rats: you may keep, breed, buy, sell, or trade a captive-bred Rattus rattus with no license or permit. The one catch is IMPORT: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26 prohibits importing the species into Alabama, so a roof rat must be acquired within the state. This supersedes the earlier, more cautious 'is it a domestic animal or a wild rodent' analysis: the agency's answer is that roof rats simply are not regulated for keeping, breeding, or selling, only their importation is barred. Never release one.
agency_confirmations: Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries Division (Capt. Jon Sims), written reply June 2026: 'We do not regulate roof rats. You can possess, buy, sale, or trade them without any license or permit. 220-2-.26 does prohibit the importation of them.' So keeping, breeding, and selling or giving a captive-bred roof rat are unregulated in Alabama (no permit), and only importing the species into the state is prohibited.

keep.why: The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries) confirmed in writing (June 2026) that Alabama does not regulate roof rats; you may possess one with no license or permit. The earlier domestic-animal-versus-wild-rodent classification question is moot: the agency does not treat a kept roof rat as a regulated 'wild rodent'.
keep.governing_law: DCNR Wildlife and Freshwater Fisheries written confirmation (June 2026): roof rats not regulated, no permit to keep. Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26 (import bar only).

breed.why: Not regulated by the state. DCNR confirmed (June 2026) you may possess, buy, sell, or trade roof rats with no license or permit, so hobby or commercial breeding needs no state wildlife permit. A storefront may still need an ordinary local business license, and federal USDA rules apply only to wholesale/sight-unseen sale (face-to-face placement is exempt).
breed.governing_law: DCNR written confirmation (June 2026): no permit to breed/possess roof rats; local business rules; USDA AWA (federal, wholesale only).

sell_give.why: DCNR confirmed (June 2026) you can buy, sell, or trade roof rats with no license or permit; free gifting is likewise unregulated. A retail storefront still needs an ordinary business license, but no wildlife or pet-dealer permit applies to the species.
sell_give.governing_law: DCNR written confirmation (June 2026): buy/sell/trade roof rats with no license or permit; ordinary business license for a storefront.

transport.why: IMPORT is prohibited. DCNR confirmed (June 2026) that Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26 prohibits importing roof rats into Alabama, so you cannot bring one in from out of state; acquire one within Alabama. Intrastate movement of a lawfully kept roof rat is not regulated (the agency does not regulate the species). Export is governed by the destination's rules, and internationally by USFWS Form 3-177 (the federal government treats R. rattus as wildlife). Never release one.
transport.governing_law: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26 (import of the species prohibited, DCNR confirmed June 2026); destination-state rules + USFWS Form 3-177 for export.

restrictions.summary: Straight from the wildlife agency (DCNR, June 2026): keeping, breeding, and selling or giving a captive-bred roof rat are unregulated in Alabama, no license or permit. The one restriction is IMPORT: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.26 bars bringing the species into the state, so acquire a roof rat within Alabama. Intrastate movement of a lawfully kept animal is not regulated. For any interstate or international export, the destination's rules and USFWS Form 3-177 apply. Never release one.
steps: Acquire a roof rat within Alabama; do not import (r. 220-2-.26 bars importing the species)
For commercial breeding or sale, check your city/county for a local business license
Never release a roof rat; rehome responsibly

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat, releasing any captive-raised/non-indigenous mammal into the wild in Alabama is illegal without express written ADCNR Commissioner permission, and it's ecologically harmful. Rehome responsibly.

inquiry_focus: We want a written interpretation of the domestic-vs-wild classification for a captive-bred, domesticated Rattus rattus kept as a pet: (a) Does ADCNR Law Enforcement recognize a pedigreed, captive-bred R. rattus that exhibits genetic docility and phenotypic variation (e.g., domestic color mutations) as a 'domestic animal' under ADPH Rule 420-4-4-.01(6), or does it categorically treat the species as a restricted 'wild rodent' under r. 220-2-.26 regardless of captive-breeding history? (b) If classified 'domestic,' is it fully exempt from the possession AND intrastate-transport bans of 220-2-.26 (so an owner needs no game-breeder license to take it to a vet)? (c) For importing a captive-bred pet roof rat into Alabama, is it treated as a standard domestic pet needing only an eCVI, or as a 'semi-wild animal' triggering the 10-day prior notice to the State Veterinarian under r. 80-3-6-.23?
